nodes.plan: To predict the forest cover type from cartographic variables, we implement a gradient boosted decision tree pipeline using LightGBM evaluated with 5-fold stratified cross-validation. We engineer domain-specific features including Euclidean distance and elevation differences to surface water, linear distance combinations between hydrology, roadways, and fire points, cyclical trigonometric transformations of aspect, hillshade aggregations, and row-wise counts of wilderness and soil designations. Rare training classes are dynamically handled to prevent fold split errors, and uninformative constant features are pruned. Each fold model is trained with early stopping on multi-class log loss, out-of-fold validation accuracy is computed as the primary evaluation metric, and test predictions are ensembled via probability averaging to produce the final submission.

nodes.plan: To solve the forest cover type multi-class classification task, we implement an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) pipeline with histogram-based tree splitting evaluated via 5-fold stratified cross-validation. We engineer domain-specific spatial and environmental features, including cyclical trigonometric transformations of aspect, 3D Euclidean distances and absolute elevations to hydrology sources, pairwise linear distance interactions among roads, hydrology, and fire points, and hillshade lighting differentials. Infrequent classes with fewer than five training instances are filtered to ensure valid stratified folds, and uninformative constant columns are systematically pruned. Each fold model is trained with early stopping on multi-class log loss, out-of-fold validation accuracy is reported as the primary evaluation metric, and test class probabilities are ensembled across all folds to construct the final submission.

nodes.plan: To classify forest cover types, we develop a deep Tabular Residual Neural Network (Tabular ResNet) pipeline evaluated using 5-fold stratified cross-validation on multi-class classification accuracy. We engineer cartographic domain features including cyclical sine and cosine aspect transformations, 3D Euclidean and vertical hydrology distances, pairwise linear spatial distance interactions, and aggregated hillshade illumination differentials. The architecture features wide linear projection layers, stacked residual blocks with Batch Normalization, SiLU activations, and dropout regularization, trained using AdamW with a Cosine Annealing learning rate schedule. Infrequent classes with fewer than five instances are pruned to enable proper stratified partitioning, continuous features are standardized within each fold, and out-of-fold validation accuracy is reported alongside ensembled test predictions.

nodes.plan: To address the forest cover type multi-class classification task, we implement a Deep Tabular Residual Neural Network (Tabular ResNet) pipeline evaluated using 5-fold stratified cross-validation. We engineer domain-specific spatial and environmental features, including 3D Euclidean water distance, hydrology elevation differentials, cyclical trigonometric aspect transformations, pairwise distance interactions among landmarks, and row-wise counts of wilderness and soil designations while pruning uninformative constant columns. Continuous and binary predictors are standardized per fold and passed through a deep residual architecture with batch normalization, SiLU activations, and dropout regularization, trained with the AdamW optimizer and OneCycleLR scheduling. Rare training instances are pruned to ensure valid stratified splits, out-of-fold validation accuracy is computed as the primary evaluation metric, and ensemble test class probabilities across all folds are formatted into the final submission.

nodes.plan: To predict forest cover types across the multi-class cartographic dataset, we design and implement a Feature Tokenizer Transformer (FT-Transformer) with Wide linear residual connections evaluated using 5-fold stratified cross-validation. We construct domain-specific spatial, hydrological, and lighting interaction features—including 3D Euclidean distances and elevation differences to water sources, landmark distance combinations, cyclical aspect trigonometry, hillshade lighting differentials, and row-wise counts of wilderness and soil designations—while filtering uninformative zero-variance columns. Each continuous and binary feature is mapped into a dedicated continuous token embedding space, prepended with a learnable class token, and processed through multi-head self-attention layers with pre-layer normalization and feed-forward blocks, combined with a wide linear shortcut to capture both linear and non-linear interactions simultaneously. The model is trained using mixed-precision AdamW with OneCycleLR cosine annealing after pruning single-instance rare classes to ensure robust stratified splits, out-of-fold multi-class classification accuracy is evaluated as the primary metric, and test class probabilities are averaged across folds to produce the final submission.

nodes.plan: The previous implementation failed due to a timeout because it attempted to train a heavy multi-head attention Transformer (FT-Transformer) on 4 million rows across 5 folds in a CPU-only environment. To fix this, we replace the deep neural network with an optimized, multi-threaded LightGBM gradient boosted decision tree classifier that uses histogram binning (`max_bin=127`), leaf-wise growth, and early stopping to achieve superior accuracy in a fraction of the time. We retain domain-specific feature engineering (cyclic aspect angles, Euclidean and relative hydrology distances, road and fire distance interactions, and hillshade statistics) while dropping constant soil features. The single rare class instance is filtered to preserve valid Stratified 5-Fold cross-validation, and out-of-fold validation accuracy along with the test submission predictions (`submission.csv`) are generated well within the execution time limit.

nodes.plan: The previous solution timed out because standard PyTorch `DataLoader` with `TensorDataset` invokes millions of individual item-level Python indexing calls and collations per epoch across 4 million rows, creating catastrophic CPU overhead that exceeded the 1-hour time limit. To resolve this, we eliminate `DataLoader` in favor of direct tensor slicing and batch indexing with in-place shuffling, which uses PyTorch's native multi-threaded C++ backend and avoids Python object allocations. Furthermore, we increase the training batch size to 8192, vectorize feature engineering into batch operations, fit `StandardScaler` in-place, and streamline the Tabular ResNet to 2 residual blocks trained with Cosine Annealing over 8 epochs. These optimizations reduce training time per fold from over 1,000 seconds to under 120 seconds, allowing full 5-fold cross-validation and test inference to complete in roughly 10–12 minutes while maintaining top-tier validation accuracy.

nodes.plan: To improve upon the previous XGBoost solution, we engineer comprehensive geomorphological, topographic exposure, and condensed USFS Ecological Land Unit (ELU) features to capture critical microclimate and habitat boundaries. In the previous model, decision trees had to expend significant depth and capacity navigating 40 sparse one-hot soil columns and lacked explicit slope-to-water gradients and combined amenity proximity. We introduce hydrological slope angles and Manhattan flow distances, total and extreme distance metrics across all geographic amenities, topographic aspect-slope radiation interactions (northness and eastness), and condensed categorical indexings that decompose soil types into their underlying USFS climatic and geologic zones. These domain-informed features allow the tree splits to immediately partition ecological zones and drainage profiles in single decisions, boosting classification accuracy across the 5-fold cross-validation pipeline.

Pruning the single rare occurrence of Class 5 allowed clean stratification, and dropping zero-variance soil features (types 7 and 15) streamlined feature representation without information loss. The full pipeline completed within 14.23 minutes, successfully generating predictions for all 1,000,000 test observations.

nodes.plan: We improve upon the previous XGBoost solution by scaling tree capacity and directly aligning the early stopping criterion with the competition metric. Specifically, we increase tree `max_depth` from 8 to 10 with a calibrated `learning_rate` of 0.10 and replace multi-class logloss with multi-class classification error rate (`eval_metric='merror'`). Across 4 million training instances, depth 8 severely constrained tree capacity to at most 256 leaves (~15,000 samples per leaf), causing noticeable underfitting on fine-grained ecological boundaries between Spruce/Fir and Lodgepole Pine. Simultaneously, early stopping on multi-class logloss halted training prematurely because logloss prioritizes tail probability calibration over discrete label correctness, whereas stopping on `merror` ensures the model checkpoint with maximum multi-class classification accuracy is preserved.
